description: What stands out about ONE boat for one week, measured against similar boats: its pros and its cons, each with how it compares ("47.9 ft (better than 99%)", "€2000 security deposit (typical €1700)", "Rare kit: [0.8%] Cool Box" — n% of those boats have it). Use when the guest asks what is special about a boat, what the catch is, why it is cheap or dear, or how it compares with others. It measures build year, length, cabins, bathrooms, guests, the security deposit and kit — and, with date_from, check-in and check-out times, the changeover day and the open weeks left; any of those it does not list is ordinary among the boats in `compared_with`, so do not sell it as an edge or a catch. Other fees are not compared. Kit is measured two ways and both hold: get_boat_details gives each item its [n%] across the whole fleet, this tool what is rare among boats like it. `rare_kit` lists that rare kit as data, most useful first, each with `useful_score` (1-5: how much it changes a charter week for the people aboard). `note` says whether an absence means "ordinary" or that nothing could be compared.

compare_by.description: Which boats count as similar. price (default): the same type priced within ±5% — what else the same money buys. guests: the same type taking the same number of guests — use when the question is value for a party size ("is it cheap for 10 people?"). length: the same type within ±2.5% of its length — use when comparing boats of one size. On guests and length the all-in day rate (the figure the search card prints) is compared too.

cutoff_pct.description: Optional, default 10, at most 50: a pro beats all but this share of the similar boats, a con trails all but it, rare kit is on fewer than it. Raise it for more, weaker lines.

date_from.description: Optional check-in date YYYY-MM-DD of the week the guest is looking at: the boats are then compared on that week's prices, and its schedule and open weeks are judged. Pass it whenever the guest has dates.

fallback.description: Optional, default true: with nothing past the cut-off on a side, name the one thing that beats (or trails) most of them. false returns only what clears the cut-off.

id.description: Boat id from search_boats or get_boat_details — copy it verbatim.

name: get_boat_standouts
title: What Stands Out About a Boat
